nodes.label: SystemLog (GRN_SystemLogs)
nodes.rationale: Table name carries a pre-existing typo (GRN_ instead of GNR_); left as-is deliberately since renaming without confirming production has the same typo would break the mapping.

nodes.label: Culture (GNR_Cultures)
nodes.rationale: Has ApplicationId in the EF model, but application code treats culture as a global, unscoped lookup (CultureServices.List()) — a deliberate mismatch flagged in the P1 architecture report.

nodes.label: UserInApplication (GNR_UserInApplications)
nodes.rationale: EF model declares a unique index on (UserId, ApplicationId), covered by SQLite tests, but not confirmed live in production; a duplicate row could still be inserted directly against SQL Server today.

nodes.label: UserAccess (GNR_UserAccesses)
nodes.rationale: Same as UserInApplication: unique (UserId, ApplicationId) index declared in EF and tested in SQLite, unconfirmed against live production.

nodes.label: Category (CMS_Categories)
nodes.rationale: ParentId self-reference is a plain int column with no FK configured in EF; hierarchy is enforced only in application code, not by the schema.

nodes.label: Comment (CMS_Comments)
nodes.rationale: Not exercised by any service in the current codebase.

nodes.label: ContentMetadata (CMS_ContentMetadata)
nodes.rationale: One-to-one with Content.

nodes.label: ContentInCategory (CMS_ContentInCategories)
nodes.rationale: Pure join row, deliberately not BaseEntity (no IsDeleted/soft-delete, no global query filter); unique on (ContentId, CategoryId) and one of only three relationships with an explicit Cascade OnDelete.

nodes.label: ContentInTag (CMS_ContentInTags)
nodes.rationale: Same shape as ContentInCategory: pure join row, not BaseEntity, unique on (ContentId, TagId), explicit Cascade.

nodes.label: ContentInCulture (CMS_ContentInCultures)
nodes.rationale: Same shape as ContentInCategory: pure join row, not BaseEntity, unique on (ContentId, CultureId), explicit Cascade.

nodes.label: BaseEntity
nodes.rationale: Shared base shape (Id, Status, IsDeleted, IsActive, CreatedDT, UpdatedDT) for every table except the three CMS_ContentIn* join tables.

nodes.label: ConfigureAudit<T> helper
nodes.rationale: Shared EF configuration helper that applies BaseEntity's audit fields and the global soft-delete filter consistently across entities, instead of repeating the configuration per entity.

nodes.label: Global EF soft-delete query filter
nodes.rationale: Added as part of the lifecycle-policy change; only exists inside the EF query pipeline, so Dapper/raw SQL (e.g. SP_ContentsInCategory) bypasses it entirely.

nodes.label: Centralize Core entity lifecycle policy (change)
nodes.rationale: Converts every application-issued delete into a soft delete (IsDeleted = true) rather than a real SQL DELETE, which makes the EF convention-default Cascade delete rules largely inert except for external hard-delete tooling.

nodes.label: inspect-schema.sql
nodes.rationale: Read-only script (SELECTs against INFORMATION_SCHEMA/sys.* only) used to confirm or refute every claim in this document against the real production schema.

nodes.label: Production baseline & migration procedure
nodes.rationale: No Migrations/ folder exists and production is externally managed and already populated, so a generated baseline migration must never be run — instead it is marked applied by manually inserting a row into __EFMigrationsHistory, after which future changes become normal, reviewed, idempotent additive migrations.

nodes.label: Optimistic concurrency (not implemented)
nodes.rationale: UpdatedDT is deliberately not marked as a concurrency token because its live SQL Server column type/precision is unverified; a dedicated rowversion column is preferred over repurposing UpdatedDT since SQL Server maintains it automatically and it cannot collide the way an app-set datetime can.

nodes.label: SP_ContentsInCategory
nodes.rationale: Its definition lives only in the production database, not in this repo; whether it filters IsDeleted/IsActive internally is unverified, and if it doesn't, a soft-deleted Content row can leak through this one read path.

nodes.label: ContentServices.GetContentsInCategory
nodes.rationale: Only gates the category (active, not-deleted, owned by caller's application) before calling the stored procedure; does not re-check IsDeleted/IsActive on each returned Content row.

nodes.label: SqlServerIntegrationTests.cs
nodes.rationale: Opt-in-only coverage against a real SQL Server, filling the gap SQLite-backed tests cannot cover; skipped by default and in CI unless a real connection string is supplied.
